In this task, you will evaluate whether each statement is supported by its corresponding citations. Note
that the system responses may appear very fluent and well-formed, but contain slight inaccuracies that are
not easy to discern at first glance. Pay close attention to the text.

You will be provided with a statement and its corresponding passage which the statement cites. It may be
helpful to ask yourself whether it is accurate to say “according to the citation ...” with the statement following this phrase. Be sure to check all of the information in the statement. You will be given three options:

• Full Support: All of the information in the statement is supported in the citation.
• Partial Support: Some parts of the information are supported in the citation, but other parts are missing.
• No Support: The citation does not support any part of the statement.

Please provide your response based on the information in the citation. If you are unsure, use your best
judgment. Respond as either “Full Support”, “Partial Support”, or “No Support” with no additional
information.
Statement: Engaging parents early and, if needed, following the school’s “interventions first, referral second” protocol, including possible OT or neurodevelopmental assessment, is advised.
Citation: Impact on Social Skills AND Behaviour
When sensory processing is disordered, it is difficult to understand situations and respond to information in the environment. This has the potential to profoundly affect a student's ability to access learning in the classroom.
If it appears that a student is experiencing sensory processing difficulties, you may consider discussing with the student's parent referral for assessment by an occupational therapist. As well as assessing the student, the occupational therapist is likely to suggest strategies for assisting the student at school. For information on general strategies which may support students with sensory processing issues, click here.

Question: What should you consider if you suspect a student has sensory processing difficulties?
Answer: Discussing with the student's parent a referral for assessment by an occupational therapist.
